theme: Logging with os.Logger: levels and subsystems

terms.definition: The Apple type from the os framework that writes messages to the system log.
terms.example: Replace print with Logger in the network layer.

terms.definition: A label such as debug, info or error that shows how important a log message is.
terms.example: The log level hides debug messages in release.
terms.code:
import os
let logger = Logger()
logger.debug("cache size 12")
logger.error("save failed")

terms.definition: A name, usually your bundle identifier, that groups the log messages from one part of your app.
terms.example: Use the bundle identifier as the subsystem.
terms.code:
import os
let logger = Logger(
    subsystem: "com.example.app",
    category: "network")

Today's terms
Logger - The Apple type from the os framework that writes messages to the system log.
Log Level - A label such as debug, info or error that shows how important a log message is.
Subsystem - A name, usually your bundle identifier, that groups the log messages from one part of your app.

landscape.description:
Explain Logger, Log Level & Subsystem in iOS by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
Logger, Log Level, Subsystem 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Logger - The Apple type from the os framework that writes messages to the system log.
한국어: Logger: os 프레임워크에서 시스템 로그에 메시지를 기록해 주는 애플의 타입

Log Level - A label such as debug, info or error that shows how important a log message is.
한국어: Log Level: debug, info, error처럼 로그 메시지의 중요도를 나타내는 라벨

Subsystem - A name, usually your bundle identifier, that groups the log messages from one part of your app.
한국어: Subsystem: 앱의 한 부분에서 나온 로그를 묶어 주는 이름으로, 보통 번들 식별자를 쓴다

In this video, Mina and Jake talk about why we use Logger instead of print, and how log levels and subsystems help, in a chat-style conversation, with the Swift code on screen.

landscape.hook: Can you explain Logger, Log Level and Subsystem in English?

dialogue.title: Better than print
dialogue.setting: Cleaning up logs in the sync code

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, my print statements are everywhere. Is there a better way to log?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, use Logger from the os framework. Logger writes messages to the system log.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It is made for apps, and you can filter and search the messages in Console.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: How do I filter the noise?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Use a log level. A log level shows how important a message is, like info or error.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So `log.info` is a normal message, and `log.error` is a problem?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. In a release build, you can hide the low log level messages.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And what is a subsystem for?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A subsystem is a name that groups your logs. We use the bundle identifier.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So I filter by subsystem and `category`?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. Pick our subsystem, then a log level, and you find the sync bug fast.

dialogue.code:
import os
let log = Logger(subsystem: "com.example.app",
                 category: "sync")
log.info("sync started")
log.error("sync failed")
